facts.statement: The only known fossil of Catenoleimus is a single coracoid bone found in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: A single species Catenoleimus anachoretus has been described, and this is only known from one piece of coracoid (specimen PO 4606), found in the Bissekty Formation of the Kyzyl Kum in present-day Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: Catenoleimus lived approximately 90 million years ago during the mid-late Turonian stage.
facts.quote: It lived during the mid-late Turonian stage, around 90 million years ago.

facts.statement: Catenoleimus was a mid-sized enantiornithine bird estimated to be 20 to 25 centimeters long.
facts.quote: This bird appears to be a mid-sized enantiornithine, perhaps 20–25 cm long in life.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone of Catenoleimus shows primitive features compared to other Enantiornithes from the same time.
facts.quote: The morphology of the bone is rather plesiomorphic compared to contemporary Enantiornithes.

facts.statement: Catenoleimus is classified within the parent group Alexornithiformes.
Catenoleimus is classified under the class Reptilia.
The fossil record for Catenoleimus spans from 93.9 to 89.8 million years ago during the Turonian.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Turonian (93.9 to 89.8 million years ago)
